A.why: Hearth-red tube with a green apron, broad block sleeves and a boxy unflared skirt; from above it reads close to the studded family.
A.fix: Bell the skirt out from the hip in widening tiers and slim the sleeves to the arm.

B.why: Clear, quiet linen bride gown that stands out at night, but the giant pale block sleeves dominate and the all-linen palette reads as the Linen family.
B.fix: Fit the sleeves close to the arm and bring wheat-gold or field green into a skirt that widens from the hip.

C.why: Almost all dark walnut with tiered pauldron-like sleeves and a split short skirt; from above it reads as lamellar armour and vanishes into the night.
C.fix: Make the skirt a single light wheat or linen bell to the ground and replace the stacked sleeve blocks with slim sleeves.

D.why: The straw hat and tiered green bell skirt with a linen apron read instantly as a farm girl's gown and a family of its own, though the sleeves are still blocks.
D.fix: Slim the grey-walnut sleeves to the arm and lighten one skirt tier or the hem so the bell stays visible at night.

E.why: Boldest flare and the most distinct family, but the high green sleeve blocks give broad shoulders and the slab tiers read as a haystack ziggurat with a kettle-hook hat.
E.fix: Slim the sleeves inside the shoulder line, merge the skirt into fewer smoother tiers and replace the hooked kerchief with a soft bonnet.

F.why: The palette and wheat wreath match the brief best, and the split wheat-gold overskirt is pretty, but bright block sleeves make it top-heavy and the skirt hangs straight.
F.fix: Slim the linen sleeves and flare both skirt layers out from the hip.

notes: No candidate fully meets the wave-2 sleeve brief: every set still uses shoulder-width block sleeves. D wins on its outline (the straw hat and tiered bell) and its zone identity. F has the best palette and headpiece but no flare. E has the flare but broad shoulders and clumsy tiers. Best next step: D's silhouette with F's wreath-and-wheat palette and slim sleeves. Judged from the sheet renders only, at 2x crops.
